correctness.rationale: For height-one connected unicyclic P the radical J has square zero and dim J=m. Choose a spanning tree to obtain a monomial isomorphism of diagonal tori with scalar G_m times the edge-weight torus satisfying the unique alternating even-cycle product relation. This yields an isomorphism over every field. Each edge commutation equation has q^2 solutions when both weights are one and q otherwise. Summing over independent pendant weights and the single cycle equation yields K=q^m+(q-2)q^(m-c+1), including q=2. Group order fixes m and the K expression is strictly decreasing in c for q>2. Degree multisets distinguish the sample posets; Stanley implies their incidence algebras cannot be (anti-)isomorphic. The independent standard-library enumerator and torus-map checks for q=2,3,4,5 all passed. Finite tests do not replace general proof.

originality.rationale: The proof supplies a common algebraic unit-group normal form indexed by the number of edges and unique cycle length, the exact conjugacy class polynomial over all finite fields, and a sharp field-order-two exception. Stanley reconstructs the poset from its associative algebra; Baclawski considers inner automorphisms of a fixed incidence algebra; Joseph and Quinn supply incidence-algebra structural background. The inspected graphical nilpotent-group enumeration is about a different graph group construction. Searches for class numbers and cross-poset group equivalence yielded no result containing or implying this theorem. Unlocated stronger literature is a residual novelty risk, not an established uniqueness claim.

value.rationale: The group of units is an intrinsic invariant of a finite associative incidence algebra. This theorem completes its isomorphism classification across a broad, natural family of unicyclic height-one posets, displays an explicit pair of associative algebras with identical unit-group schemes, and proves their unique cycle lengths can nevertheless be recovered from finite-field group conjugacy statistics when q>2. At q=2 the boundary is exact: only number of edges survives. The constrained cycle interaction is not obtained by repeating the earlier forest case.
